outcomes.text: Perform a solo piece on any instrument or voice where your part is distinctive and leading.
Perform with the written accompaniment kept intact, or over a backing track without your part audible in it.
Perform in an ensemble with undoubled, independent, simultaneous parts.
Balance your part with others and react and adjust to them while playing.
Interpret music with technical control, phrasing and dynamics that suit its style and mood.
Perform live, unedited and uninterrupted, by playing, singing, improvising or realising music with technology.
Perform from a score with accurate pitch, rhythm, intonation and tuning, and follow all performance directions.
Understand the contextual influences on the pieces performed, including the composer's intentions.
Improvise accurately, developing the music's potential with good tone, technique and structure.
Perform music passed on by oral tradition, such as ballads, songs or chants.
Rap with clear diction and breath control, or beatbox with contrasting timbres and secure rhythm.
Perform a live line using synthesisers, effects or loop pedals, with or without a backing track.

topics.title: Musical elements, contexts and language in performing

outcomes.text: Use pitch, tonality, structure, sonority, texture, tempo-metre-rhythm and dynamics appropriately in performance.
Consider purpose, audience, time and place when performing, and read staff notation and chord symbols.
Develop musical ideas into compositions or arrangements.

subtopics.title: Writing for instruments, voices and technology

outcomes.text: Write idiomatically for instruments, voices or technology, handling timbre and texture sensitively.
Build rhythmic, melodic and harmonic construction within chosen forms and structures.
Develop the technical skills to meet a brief and relate it to its audience and occasion.
Notate a composition using staff notation, graphic notation or a written account.
Use the musical elements, context of purpose and audience, and correct musical language in composing.
Develop a given melody into a piece for one instrument and accompaniment using forms like binary, ternary, rondo and variations.
Use repetition, variation, extension and motivic working to sustain a piece.
Set words to music for voice and accompaniment, linking song form (strophic, da capo, verse/chorus) to the text.

subtopics.title: Brief 3: Music for Stage and Screen

outcomes.text: Compose a soundtrack for a scenario by underscoring action and creating flowing moods and atmospheres.
Combine music, lyrics and dance in a show song.
Compose a piece based on two set styles by combining harmony, melody, rhythm and instrumentation for each style's feel.
Compose a free piece of your own, drawing on set works, wider listening and the intended audience or occasion.
Describe form, structure, stylistic features and conventions of music, and how it relates to its context.
Express and justify opinions and preferences about music using correct vocabulary.
Identify melody and harmony devices, simple chord progressions and cadences, and major, minor, modal, pentatonic and chromatic tonalities.
Recognise structures such as verse-chorus, call and response, binary and variations, and textures like monophony, homophony and polyphony.
Identify instruments, playing techniques, articulation and effects, and how they are used to good effect.
Recognise pulse, simple and compound time, and devices like syncopation, swung and dotted rhythms and triplets.
Recognise crescendo and diminuendo and devices such as ostinato, riff, imitation, pedal, drone and sequence.
Explain how purpose, intention, audience, time and place shape how music is made and performed.
Read and write treble and bass clef, simple time rhythms, key signatures to four sharps or flats, and chord symbols.
Use accurate music terminology, such as ostinato versus riff, and score terms like continuo.

topics.title: Areas of study and set works

outcomes.text: Study Bach's Brandenburg Concerto no. 5 (3rd movement), including Baroque features and fugue in a gigue.
Study Beethoven's Piano Sonata no. 8 'Pathetique' (1st movement) in sonata form.
Study Purcell's Music for a While as a Baroque setting for voice and accompaniment.
Study Queen's Killer Queen as a twentieth-century song for voice and accompaniment.
Study Schwartz's Defying Gravity from Wicked as musical theatre.
Study Williams's Star Wars main title to see how film music is composed to picture.
Study Afro Celt Sound System's Release and see how two cultures' elements combine in a fusion.
Study Esperanza Spalding's Samba Em Preludio as a fusion creating a new style.
Listen perceptively to unfamiliar music, placing its genre, composer and date in context.
Recognise chords and keys and complete musical dictation tasks.
Compare a set work extract with an unfamiliar piece, evaluating elements, contexts and language and reaching a conclusion.
